reader.requirement: At --std 85 a SOURCE identifier-1 must be a valid MOVE sender to its printable item under the 1985 MOVE rules: an index data item is refused (VI.6.19.3 SR4), the elementary moves GR3 a-c forbid (alphabetic or alphanumeric-edited to numeric/numeric-edited, numeric to alphabetic, noninteger numeric to alphanumeric/alphanumeric-edited) are refused, and every other move (group, de-editing, alphanumeric to numeric, reference-modified, ODO group, counters) is accepted and performed as a MOVE.

refuter.evidence: Checked the reader's de-editing moves against §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3d ('In level 1 a numeric edited data item must not be moved to a numeric or numeric edited data item'). The rule is level 1 only, and the de-editing of GR4b is the level-2 boxed text this full implementation takes, so the reader's accepted ZZ9.99 -> ZZ9.99 stands. rw_src_bad2.cob at 85: numeric-edited -> A(3) (GR3b), 9V9 -> XBX (GR3c, alphanumeric-edited receiver), scaled PP9 -> X(3) (noninteger via P), and A(3) -> ZZ9 each gave COBOL2770, exit 65 (plus an unrelated COBOL0900 on my own numeric-edited VALUE). rw_src_ok3.cob (legal, exit 0) wrote the report line '1200 045 0 0 7    -45 1234 001': integer scaled 99PP -> X(4) = 1200; S9(3) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -45 -> X(3) = 045, the sign not moved and the size one less (GR4a); 007 -> XBXBX = '0 0 7'; -45 -> -(5)9; COMP 1234 -> X(4); LINE-COUNTER -> 9(3). cite.py: OK  §1985:XIII.3.18.3 SR2  (3.18.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2; OK  §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3d  (6.19.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3d; OK  §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3b ...; OK  §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3c ...
